You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL-openclaw-luna6-high-ws0/frozen/seen/play/users/u030/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL-openclaw-luna6-high-ws0/frozen/seen/play/users/u030/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.
1. When an instance starts, look for the task's file. If it exists, run its transform on the test input and submit the result before anything else.
2. If there is no file, or its answer was wrong, request demonstration pairs as you judge necessary, write or fix transform, and run it on every pair you have received until it reproduces all of them; then submit its output for the test input. Checking a program on the pairs is free.
3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all the pairs to the task's file, replacing any older version, then finish.

---
name: continual-arc
description: "Solve Continual-ARC grid instances: reuse task programs, infer transforms from demos, and submit verified outputs."
---

# Continual ARC

1. At instance start, check `programs/<task id>.py`. If present, run `transform(test_grid)` and submit its returned grid before requesting demos or changing the program.
2. If the program is absent or its answer is rejected, request only the demonstrations needed to infer the rule. Separate structural clues from exact cell placement: for expansions, compare dimensions, preserved regions, block histograms, then positions; matching histograms proves only a permutation. For sparse, interrupted outlines, check whether markers trace an enclosing frame before filling gaps; if so, fill only missing border cells. For diagonal stripe patterns, compare cells by `r+c` and `r-c` to identify the stripe direction, then read demonstrated outputs along that diagonal index to infer the cycle, phase, and any unequal run widths. A period that merely fits sparse clues does not determine unseen colors: request another demo rather than filling unknown residues by guess or nearest-neighbor. Implement or fix `transform(grid)` and run it against every exact pair received; require exact input-output matches before submitting. When transcribing grids for local testing, assert row count and every row width against the stated dimensions; fix transcription errors before trusting results.
3. Run the verified transform on the test input and copy its returned grid exactly into the required submit action; do not manually adjust cells. Keep the required action JSON as the final line.
4. After verdict, save the transform that reproduces all received pairs at `programs/<task id>.py`, replacing the old version, then finish only when the instance is over.
